newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks inch down in sluggish Monday start.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks inch down in sluggish Monday start.

text.p: Mexican stocks opened very marginally down on what traders said was a typically slow Monday morning start amid a market awaiting developments on Wall Street.
"I think everyone is still asleep, or waiting for a definite trend from the Dow Jones and for the heavyweights to open," a floor trader said.
The leading IPC share index was off 2.30 point in the opening minutes of trade, or 0.06 percent, at 3,871.80. Trading activity was sleepwalking at just 382,000 shares.
"There's a tiny bit of selling, but most blue chips have opened flat," the trader added.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average was up 32.97 points at 7,202.50.
Dealers drew attention to the fact that Telmex, normally the bourse's most heavily traded stock, had yet to open in Mexico. On Wall Street, the telecom firm's ADRs were meanwhile up 1/4 at 42-3/8.
On the broad market, 22 stocks had traded, of which sliders outstripped gainers by seven to four.
Steel tube maker Tamsa headed the short gainers' list, up 50 centavos to 134.50 pesos, while leading decliner was holding company Femsa, down 50 centavos at 40.50 pesos.
Dealers said volume was too thin to denote any fundamental market trends.
"There are no investors in the market yet, just in-and-out trading," a desk trader said.
